note: Tier 2 — the curated constant set (ADR-0001). Hand-maintained: unlike tier1.json this file is authored rather than generated, and editing it is the intended way to change it. Every scalar is a decimal string for the same reason node totals are (SPEC-0002 REQ "Exact Quantity Encoding").
verified_meaning: A constant's `verified` is the date it was confirmed in game, or null for one that has not been. Null is not a placeholder for missing metadata: the engine reads a constant with no verified date as unverified and taints every figure derived from it, which is why nothing here is presented as fact. Filling one in is how a figure stops carrying the unverified badge.

biodomeCropSlots.source: docs/design/base-planner/handoff.md records 'dome capacity 16' as illustrative, and the community wiki reports the same. ADR-0001 searched the reality tables and found no field that states it.
biodomeCropSlots.note: May be geometric — snap points in the scene — and so extractable after all, in which case this entry moves to Tier 1.

faunaYieldPerCycle.source: Not in the reality tables. Fauna products come from creature data the Tier 1 pipeline does not read (ADR-0001 § Tier 2).
faunaYieldPerCycle.note: Placeholder, chosen conservatively: one unit per creature per cycle sizes a ranch upward rather than downward, so a plan built on it over-provisions instead of coming up short.

faunaCycleSeconds.source: As above — creature data this pipeline does not read.
faunaCycleSeconds.note: Placeholder. Thirty minutes is the figure the test fixtures have used; nothing has confirmed it in game.

stepsPerProcessor.source: ADR-0001 § Tier 2 — 'how hard to work one machine', a planner policy rather than missing game data.
stepsPerProcessor.note: One step per processor: the plan never asks one machine to cover two steps. The unambiguous reading, and changeable here without touching code.

depotThreshold.source: docs/design/base-planner/handoff.md — 'supply depots (720u) when qty > 360'. ADR-0001 § Tier 2 records it as policy: the game has no opinion about when hoarding starts.
depotThreshold.note: Depot *capacity* is not here. That is U_SILO_S's storage buffer, which tier1.json carries.

processSeconds.source: Economy.Refining states nutrient processor throughput per cycle but not the cycle's duration, so the duration is supplied here.

panelsPerBattery.source: docs/design/base-planner/handoff.md — solar 'adds 1 battery per 2 panels for night coverage'. ADR-0001 notes the battery *capacity* is extractable but the ratio is not.
panelsPerBattery.note: A choice about how much darkness to plan for, not a game constant.

faunaProducts.source: The FOOD_V_* family in tier1.json is what a creature yields when it is fed. The one member excluded is FOOD_V_BUG, whose default_method is 'cook' — it is produced, not harvested.
faunaProducts.note: Classification, not a scalar: the engine has no verified-date slot for it, so these ids change which producer row a leaf gets rather than whether a figure is verified. An id absent here is sized as a crop or an extractor instead.

resourceHotspots.source: The three gas-hotspot resources and the ten planetary minerals a Mineral Extractor draws. Nothing in the searched tables maps an item to a hotspot category — a part declares DependsOnHotspots, the item does not — so this is supplied rather than inferred from the item's name.
resourceHotspots.note: Deliberately partial, and partial is safe: an item with no category here is refused by name (MISSING_CONSTANT, 'no hotspot category is configured for X') rather than sized against a guessed one. Add an id when you have confirmed the resource is hotspot-extractable, not when a plan happens to want it.
